rules.title: Modules loaded in dependency order, root last
rules.statement: Compiling a root file transitively resolves and parses all files reachable through `use <pkg>;` declarations; the resulting module sequence is topologically ordered with every dependency preceding any module that uses it and the root module last.

rules.title: `use` resolves a dotted package to a source file via search paths
rules.statement: A `use <pkg>;` declaration is resolved by locating the file for the dotted package name `pkg` within the configured search directories; failure to resolve any `use` is an error (B-mv-03/04) reported per declaration.

rules.title: Module package is a dotted name; may be empty
rules.statement: Each module carries a dotted package name (e.g. `std.io`); a plain user program with no package declaration has an empty package name.

rules.title: No owning module ⇒ no module-qualified mangling
rules.statement: A module's owning-MODULE identity is the unit of distribution it belongs to: `module_id` is the mangle key and `module_name` the canonical handle. A plain user program (no module) has empty identity, which disables module-qualified symbol mangling for its items.

rules.title: Binary-archive modules keep their original prelude
rules.statement: Files loaded from a binary archive are never re-augmented with the consumer's implicit prelude; the prelude in effect at their original build time is final.

rules.title: Excluded path prefixes are not picked up as source
rules.statement: Absolute path prefixes declared as excludes (mirroring the manifest `exclude` directive) remove matching files from the text-package index: a `use` whose resolution begins with an excluded prefix is not loaded from source, deferring that package to a binary archive instead.

rules.title: Modules may be loaded from binary `.writ0` archives
rules.statement: A module may be loaded from a precompiled `.writ0` member inside a `.a` archive rather than from source; binary modules take their `module_id`/`module_name` from the archive's `@module` `.pkgi` header.

rules.title: Lazy archives are lowered as local code
rules.statement: A lazy-mode binary archive ships only the parsed AST (no object text, no LIR blob); the consumer must lower such a module's items locally (sema/mono/codegen treat them as user code).

rules.title: Stdlib export catalog lists exactly the generic items
rules.statement: A binary module's exports catalog records precisely the items whose `type_params` is non-empty (generic struct/enum/fn templates); non-generic items are not catalogued as templates.

rules.title: Blanket impls catalogued by trait and bounds
rules.statement: An exported blanket impl `impl<T: Bound + Extra...> Trait for T` is catalogued as (trait, primary bound, extra bounds), with the target type being the type variable by definition; an unbounded blanket impl has empty primary bound.

rules.title: Concrete-impl catalog excludes negative and DST-target impls
rules.statement: An exported concrete impl `impl Trait for Target` is catalogued as (trait, target); negative impls and DST target patterns are dropped from the catalog (which is a fast-path lookup index only, not the authoritative impl set).

rules.title: Export merge across archives is order-preserving, later wins on fn duplicate
rules.statement: When export catalogs from multiple archives are unioned, archive order is preserved and a later archive wins on a duplicate function-template mangled symbol (occurs only when a project redefines a stdlib mangled symbol).
